text_to_image: First-person perspective. The protagonist is holding a small mechanical toy in one hand. Below the hand is a wooden table that fully covers the background. The toy is small enough to fit perfectly in one hand and is currently in its untransformed state. It is a compact, tapered sleek teardrop-shaped object made of brushed titanium and iridescent blue enamel, silver micro-servos and delicate link chains. The toy features a tiny raised silver stud behind the dorsal ridge. Soft diffused daylight from the upper left, shallow depth of field. Photorealistic, ultra-detailed, high quality.
image_to_video: First-person perspective, filmed in one continuous long take, strictly no cuts or camera transitions allowed. The camera remains steady and does not move. The protagonist presses the tiny silver stud on the upper ridge with their finger, then places the toy onto the wooden table below. The transformation begins immediately and completes fully within the shot. The toy begins unfolding and transforming until it becomes the form of a miniature mechanical flying fish. The unfolding and transformation process is logical and physically consistent. The sleek teardrop body divides along its ventral line and the upper flanks swing upward like pectoral fin shrouds, revealing the movement of internal mechanical components and gears. Two expansive lattice pectoral fins and a fine needle-like tail physically push out into place. The transformation process is relatively simple and not overly complicated. Strictly no parts appear or disappear out of nowhere. After transformation, the final mechanical flying fish's size remains believable and perfectly consistent with what the original toy could realistically unfold into, with absolutely no magical volume expansion. Audio: crisp mechanical clicks, servo whirs and ratcheting gears, ending with a soft metallic latch as the transformation completes. No music, no voice.
